notes.definition: A formulation is a mixture that has been designed as a useful product. It is made by mixing several components in carefully measured quantities so that the product has exactly the properties it needs.
explanation: Many everyday products are complex mixtures in which each chemical has a particular purpose. These products are called formulations. A formulation is not just any mixture: it has been deliberately designed, and the amount of each component is measured carefully. Changing the proportions changes the properties of the product, so manufacturers follow a precise 'recipe' every time.

Paint is a good example. It contains a pigment to give colour, a binder that holds the pigment and sticks it to the surface as a film, a solvent that keeps the paint runny so it can be spread (and then evaporates), and additives such as preservatives or substances that help it dry. If there were too little binder, the paint would rub off; too much solvent and it would drip.

Other formulations include fuels (petrol contains hydrocarbons plus additives that help it burn smoothly), cleaning agents (detergents, water softeners, fragrances), medicines (the active ingredient plus fillers, binders, flavourings and coatings), alloys (metals mixed with other elements to make them harder or more resistant to corrosion), fertilisers (mixtures of compounds supplying nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium in chosen ratios) and foods (ingredients plus preservatives, emulsifiers and colourings).

In a medicine, the active ingredient is the drug that has the effect on the body. It may be only a small fraction of the tablet's mass. The rest of the formulation helps the tablet hold together, dissolve at the right rate, be easy to swallow and taste acceptable. Because the dose matters, the quantity of active ingredient in every tablet must be the same, which is why formulations need careful measurement.

In exams you may be given information about a product and asked whether it is a formulation. Look for these features: it is a mixture; it has been designed for a particular use; each component has a specific job; and the components are present in fixed, measured amounts. A random mixture such as muddy water or air is not a formulation, because it is not designed and its proportions are not controlled.
keyFacts: A formulation is a mixture designed as a useful product.
Formulations are made by mixing components in carefully measured quantities.
Each component in a formulation has a particular purpose.
Examples: fuels, cleaning agents, paints, medicines, alloys, fertilisers and foods.
Changing the proportions of the components changes the properties of the product.
Paint: pigment (colour), binder (sticks pigment to surface), solvent (makes it spreadable), additives.
In a medicine, the active ingredient is the drug; the other components help make it usable.
A formulation is impure in the chemical sense because it is a mixture.

keyTerms.definition: A mixture that has been designed as a useful product, made by mixing components in carefully measured quantities.
One of the substances that make up a mixture or formulation.
The substance in a medicine (or other product) that produces the intended effect.
A substance in paint or ink that gives it its colour.
The component of paint that holds the pigment particles together and makes them stick to a surface.
The liquid in which other components are dissolved or dispersed; in paint it evaporates as the paint dries.
A mixture of a metal with other elements (usually metals), designed to have improved properties such as hardness.

equations.name: Percentage of a component
equations.formula: percentage of component = (mass of component ÷ total mass) × 100

equations.name: Mass of a component
equations.units: same units as the total mass (g or kg)

workedExamples.title: Mass of a component in a formulation
workedExamples.question: A paint formulation contains 15% pigment by mass. Calculate the mass of pigment in a 4.0 kg tin of paint.

workedExamples.title: Percentage of the active ingredient
workedExamples.question: A tablet has a mass of 600 mg. It contains 500 mg of paracetamol (the active ingredient). Calculate the percentage by mass of paracetamol in the tablet.

workedExamples.title: Identifying a formulation
workedExamples.question: Which is a formulation: (a) sea water or (b) a washing-up liquid containing 15% detergent, 1% fragrance, 0.5% preservative and water? Explain.
steps: A formulation is a mixture designed as a useful product, with components in measured quantities.
Sea water is a natural mixture; its proportions are not designed or controlled.
Washing-up liquid has components in fixed percentages, each with a purpose (cleaning, smell, keeping it fresh).
workedExamples.answer: (b) washing-up liquid is a formulation; sea water is a mixture but not a formulation.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think any mixture is a formulation.
misconceptions.right: In fact a formulation is a mixture that has been designed for a use, with each component in a carefully measured quantity. Air or sea water are mixtures but not formulations.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think a medicine tablet is made only of the drug.
misconceptions.right: In fact the active ingredient may be a small part of the tablet; fillers, binders, coatings and flavourings make up the rest.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think that because a formulation is carefully made it is 'pure'.
misconceptions.right: In fact a formulation is a mixture, so in chemistry it is not a pure substance.

misconceptions.wrong: Students often think the exact proportions in a formulation do not matter much.
misconceptions.right: In fact changing the proportions changes the properties, for example too much solvent makes paint runny and too little active ingredient makes a medicine ineffective.

realWorld: Paracetamol tablets contain the drug plus starch and other ingredients so the tablet holds together and dissolves in the stomach.
Fertilisers are sold with labels giving N:P:K ratios, chosen for lawns, flowers or crops.
Petrol contains additives that improve combustion and protect engines; the formulation is changed for summer and winter.
Solder, brass and stainless steel are alloys designed with precise compositions for their uses.
examTips: To identify a formulation, use the key phrases: 'mixture', 'designed as a useful product', 'components in measured quantities', 'each component has a purpose'.
You do not need to remember specific formulations; use the information in the question to say what each component does.
In percentage calculations, check the percentages of all components add up to 100% and that your answer has the same units as the total mass.
If asked why quantities must be measured carefully, say that the product must have the required properties every time (for example the same dose in every tablet).
summary: A formulation is a mixture designed as a useful product.
Components are mixed in carefully measured quantities.
Each component has a specific purpose.
Examples: fuels, cleaning agents, paints, medicines, alloys, fertilisers, foods.

questions.question: What is a formulation?
options: A pure compound made in a laboratory
A mixture that has been designed as a useful product
Any mixture of two or more substances
A compound made by a chemical reaction
markScheme: 1 mark: A mixture that has been designed as a useful product
questions.explanation: A formulation is specifically a designed mixture with components in measured amounts. Not every mixture is a formulation, and a formulation is not a single compound.

questions.question: Which of these is a formulation?
options: Sea water
Air
Crude oil
Hand cream
markScheme: 1 mark: Hand cream
questions.explanation: Hand cream is designed for a purpose, with ingredients in measured amounts. Sea water, air and crude oil are natural mixtures.

questions.question: What is the job of the pigment in a paint?
options: It gives the paint its colour
It makes the paint dry quickly
It sticks the paint to the wall
It makes the paint runny
markScheme: 1 mark: It gives the paint its colour
questions.explanation: The pigment gives colour. The binder sticks it to the surface and the solvent makes it runny.

questions.question: Why are the components of a formulation mixed in carefully measured quantities?
options: So that it becomes a pure substance
So that the components react to form a new compound
So that the product has the required properties
So that it can be separated easily later
markScheme: 1 mark: So that the product has the required properties
questions.explanation: The proportions determine the properties of the product. The components are mixed, not reacted, and the product is a mixture, not a pure substance.

questions.question: In a paint, which component evaporates as the paint dries?
options: Pigment
Binder
Solvent
Additive
markScheme: 1 mark: Solvent
questions.explanation: The solvent keeps paint liquid for spreading and then evaporates, leaving the pigment held by the binder.

questions.question: A tablet contains an active ingredient, starch, a sweetener and a coating. What is the active ingredient?
options: The substance that makes the tablet taste sweet
The substance that holds the tablet together
The substance that makes the tablet easy to swallow
The drug that has the effect on the body
markScheme: 1 mark: The drug that has the effect on the body
questions.explanation: The active ingredient is the drug. The other components are there to make the tablet hold together, taste better and be easy to swallow.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT listed by AQA as an example of a formulation?
options: Rainwater
Alloy
Fuel
Fertiliser
markScheme: 1 mark: Rainwater
questions.explanation: Rainwater is not a designed product. Fertilisers, alloys and fuels are formulations.

questions.question:
A company changes the formulation of its washing-up liquid.
Table 1 shows the old and new formulations.
Which statement is correct?
options: The product is now a pure substance
The product is no longer a formulation
The properties of the product, such as cleaning power, will change
The detergent will react with the water to form a new compound
markScheme: 1 mark: The properties of the product, such as cleaning power, will change
questions.explanation: Changing proportions changes properties; it is still a designed mixture (formulation), not a pure substance, and no new compound is formed.

questions.question: Which statement best explains why steel used for cutlery is described as a formulation?
options: It is made of a single element
It is a mixture of iron with set amounts of chromium, nickel and carbon designed to resist corrosion
Its components are chemically bonded in a compound
It is a natural ore of iron
markScheme: 1 mark: It is a mixture of iron with set amounts of chromium, nickel and carbon designed to resist corrosion
questions.explanation: An alloy is a designed mixture with measured composition. It is not a single element or a compound.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the composition of a paint.
Calculate the mass of pigment in 2.5 kg of the paint.
markScheme: 1 mark: 0.5 kg
questions.explanation: 0.20 × 2.5 = 0.50 kg. Remember to convert the percentage to a decimal before multiplying.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the components of a paracetamol tablet.
Calculate the percentage by mass of paracetamol in the tablet.
Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
questions.explanation: 500 ÷ 600 = 0.8333; × 100 = 83.3%. The other 16.7% is made up of other components such as fillers and binders.

questions.question:
A bag of fertiliser has a mass of 50 kg.
Ammonium nitrate makes up 34% of the mass.
Calculate the mass of ammonium nitrate in the bag.
markScheme: 1 mark: 17 kg
questions.explanation: Convert 34% to 0.34, then 0.34 × 50 kg = 17 kg of ammonium nitrate.

questions.question:
18 carat gold is an alloy that is 75% gold by mass.
A ring made from 18 carat gold contains 4.5 g of gold.
Calculate the total mass of the ring.
markScheme: 1 mark: 4.5 g is 75% of the total
1 mark: 6.0 g
questions.explanation: Rearrange: total mass = mass of gold ÷ (75 ÷ 100) = 4.5 ÷ 0.75 = 6.0 g. A common error is to multiply 4.5 by 0.75.

questions.question:
A cleaning spray is made by adding 5.0 cm³ of concentrate to water to make a total volume of 250 cm³.
Calculate the percentage by volume of concentrate in the spray.
markScheme: 1 mark: 2.0%
questions.explanation: 5.0 ÷ 250 = 0.020; × 100 = 2.0%. Use the total volume (250 cm³), not the volume of water added.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the composition of a paint.
Calculate the percentage by mass of pigment in the paint.
markScheme: 1 mark: 20%
questions.explanation: All components must add up to 100%, so pigment = 100 − 80 = 20%.

questions.question: Give the definition of a formulation.
acceptedAnswers: mixture designed as a useful product
markScheme: 1 mark: a mixture that has been designed as a useful product
questions.explanation: Both 'mixture' and 'designed as a useful product' are needed.

questions.question: Name two types of product that are formulations.
markScheme: 1 mark each for any two of: fuels, cleaning agents, paints, medicines, alloys, fertilisers, foods (max 2)
questions.explanation: These are the examples named in the AQA specification. Many specific products (toothpaste, shampoo, sun cream) are also correct.

questions.question:
Table 1 shows the components of a sun cream.
Explain why sun cream is described as a formulation.
markScheme: 1 mark: it is a mixture designed as a useful product
1 mark: the components are present in measured/fixed quantities, each with a particular purpose
questions.explanation: Both ideas show it is a deliberately designed mixture rather than a random one.

rows: Stops the oil and water separating

questions.question: Suggest what would happen to a paint if it contained too little binder. Explain your answer.
markScheme: 1 mark: the paint would not stick well / would rub off or flake
1 mark: because the binder holds the pigment together and sticks it to the surface
questions.explanation: Each component has a job, so changing its amount changes the product's properties.

questions.question: Explain why every tablet of a medicine must contain exactly the same mass of active ingredient.
markScheme: 1 mark: so each tablet gives the correct/same dose
1 mark: too little would not work; too much could be harmful
questions.explanation: Medicines are formulations because the dose of drug must be controlled precisely.

questions.question: A student says: 'Muddy water is a formulation because it is a mixture.' Explain whether the student is correct.
markScheme: 1 mark: not correct (muddy water is a mixture but not a formulation)
1 mark: it has not been designed as a product and the quantities of components are not measured/controlled
questions.explanation: Being a mixture is necessary but not enough. A formulation must be designed with measured proportions.

questions.question: Suggest one reason why a manufacturer would add a preservative to a food or cosmetic formulation, and one reason why the amount added is carefully controlled.
markScheme: 1 mark: to stop microorganisms growing / so the product lasts longer
1 mark: too much could be harmful or change the product's properties (taste, smell); too little would not work
questions.explanation: This applies the idea that every component has a purpose and is present in a measured amount.

questions.question: Paint is a formulation containing a pigment, a binder, a solvent and additives. Describe the purpose of each component and explain why paint is a formulation.
markScheme: Indicative content: pigment gives colour
Binder holds the pigment together and sticks it to the surface, forming a film
Solvent dissolves/disperses the other components so paint can be spread; it evaporates as paint dries
Additives give extra properties, for example faster drying or preservation
Paint is a mixture designed as a useful product
Components are in carefully measured proportions to give the right properties
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): purposes of at least three components given and clear explanation of why paint is a formulation
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): one or two purposes given, or a simple statement that paint is a mixture
questions.explanation: Full answers explain both what each part does and the defining features of a formulation.

questions.question:
A pharmaceutical company makes ibuprofen tablets.
Table 1 shows the components of one tablet.
Explain why the tablet is a formulation, why it is not a pure substance in the chemical sense, and why the company must measure the quantity of each component carefully.
Include a calculation of the percentage by mass of ibuprofen in the tablet.
markScheme: Indicative content: the tablet is a mixture designed as a useful product (a medicine)
Each component has a purpose: ibuprofen is the active ingredient; starch adds bulk and helps it break up; the binder holds it together; the coating makes it easier to swallow and masks taste
It is not chemically pure because it contains more than one compound (a pure substance is one element or compound only)
It would melt over a range of temperatures, unlike a pure substance
Percentage of ibuprofen = (200 ÷ 400) × 100 = 50%
Quantities must be measured so every tablet contains the correct dose
Too little active ingredient: ineffective; too much: risk of harm
Wrong amounts of binder or coating would change how the tablet holds together or dissolves
Level 3 (5 to 6 marks): all three explanations given clearly with correct calculation and linked reasoning
Level 2 (3 to 4 marks): two explanations with some detail, or calculation plus one explanation
Level 1 (1 to 2 marks): simple relevant statements
questions.explanation: The best answers link the definitions of formulation and pure substance to the specific tablet and support the argument about measurement with the 50% calculation.

questions.question: Petrol contains a mixture of hydrocarbons together with small, measured amounts of additives to help it burn smoothly. What is petrol?
options: A pure compound
A simple compound of carbon and hydrogen
An element
A formulation
markScheme: 1 mark: A formulation
questions.explanation: Petrol is a mixture designed as a useful product with additives in measured quantities, so it is a formulation.

questions.question: What is meant by the 'active ingredient' in a medicine?
markScheme: 1 mark: the substance (drug) that has the medical effect on the body
questions.explanation: Other components in a tablet make it easier to make, store and take, but do not treat the illness.

questions.question: Which of these is an example of a formulation?
options: Toothpaste
Distilled water
Pure gold
Oxygen
markScheme: 1 mark: Toothpaste
questions.explanation: Toothpaste is a designed mixture of abrasives, fluoride, detergent, flavouring and water in measured amounts.
